display.title: Hillel on the Roof
display.summary_short: Young Hillel loves Torah so much that he lies on the shul's snowy skylight in a blizzard to hear the lesson below, and is found nearly frozen.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi tells of the great Hillel when he was a young scholar. Long ago, before radiators, homes and shuls were heated with wood from the forest. In one town, a large shul was full of Torah scholars learning day and night, and in winter everyone brought a few logs of firewood as a kind of entrance fee. Hillel learned all day, supported by kind people, and could not bear to take time away from learning to chop wood, yet he was too honest to come in without it. On a freezing morning in a blizzard, he climbed onto the roof and lay on the glass skylight so he could hear the lesson. When a student went up to sweep away the snow, he found Hillel lying motionless under a blanket of snow. They carried him inside and warmed him by the fire, and he opened his eyes and apologized for the trouble. The townspeople asked his forgiveness and freed him from bringing wood. Hillel grew up to be the famous Hillel of the Mishnah and Pirkei Avos, the head of Beis Hillel.
display.lesson: Love Torah so much that you are ready to give up your comfort to learn more.

date.note: Date of episode 425 (Lag BaOmer 'Sunday, May 13' and candle times). The same story first aired in episode 375 (2 May 1989).

advisories.note: Hillel is found motionless under the snow and the townspeople fear he has frozen; he revives.
